newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Three Thai companies postpone ethylene projects.
newsitem.headline: Three Thai companies postpone ethylene projects.

text.p: Three Thai companies have postponed plans to build large ethylene plants in the face of the country's ongoing economic problems, industry sources said on Thursday.
Officials at National Petrochemical Corp (NPC) and Thai Petrochemical Industry (TPI) said they have shelved plans to build the plants in 1999 indefinitely.
Industry sources said a third project mooted by Bangkok Bank has also been shelved. Bangkok Bank officials could not be reached for confirmation.
"Since the economy has slowed down, we will carry out this project (new) in the future," a TPI source said.
Analysts say the three projects are now expected to start up after 2001.
The Thai Board of Investment in May granted investment incentives to TPI Olefins Co, a unit of TPI, for the building of the 14-billion baht (US$485 million) petrochemical complex.
At the core of the complex is a 700,000 tonne-per-year (tpa) ethylene plant due to come onstream by end 1999.
The TPI officials said the company would instead "try to debottleneck the first plant" before embarking on the major expansion.
TPI started up its first 350,000-tpa ethylene plant in February 1997.
Thailand's pioneer petrochemical company, NPC said it will concentrate on building value added plants that make use of existing ethylene feedstock.
NPC operates a 410,000-tpa ethylene plant and had planned to build the new plant in 1999.
